scope: Desktop cartridge-backup file publication: force and close a sibling temporary before atomic rename; refuse unsupported atomic replacement

behavior.owner: The emulation caller snapshots its own backup. IO receives owned bytes and markSaved occurs only after successful publication.
behavior.prepublication_failure: Prior save remains byte-identical, or no target is created; pending backup remains dirty. Retry publishes the full snapshot.
behavior.unsupported_atomic_move: Actionable IOException. No non-atomic fallback, previous save preserved.
behavior.lost_acknowledgement_after_rename: A complete new target may already be present; report the failure, keep pending backup dirty, permit retry. No rollback to stale data.
behavior.cleanup_failure: Keep the primary IO error and attach cleanup as a suppressed exception. Orphan temporaries are never adopted by load.
behavior.durability_scope: FileChannel.force(true) precedes close and rename. No simulated process or physical power-loss guarantee, no parent-directory sync qualification.

tests.matrix: 8 failures x first publication / replacement = 16 cases
other_cases: cleanup failure retains primary error and committed file; fresh load ignores partial temporary; retry succeeds
force plus close failures retain suppression order
tests.storage: Real temp files and real disk writer; composition injects one failure at the IO boundary. No vendor tools or player assets required.

validation.sdk_rebuild: Not required: only desktop storage and host tests changed; portable/MIDP sources and state format are unchanged.

game_replay.route: LeafGreen USA Rev-A counter-0 seed -> move left -> counter-1 save

report.qualification: headless-only; physical presentation and playback unverified
report.hardware: Linux x86_64 cloud host; deterministic counter-wrap route, no physical presentation measurement

game_replay.strict_reference_gate: Existing full RGB/PCM and whole-save differences against mGBA remain unchanged; this validates host file publication only.

reproduction.real_game: Repeat save-one from the counter-wrap record with an owned copy of the counter-0 seed and fresh output. Compare all frames.jsonl bytes, audio.wav bytes and the final 128 KiB save to the baseline.
